cards.explanation: The answer is whether he will recover from this illness. Ben-hadad, king of Aram, tells his man Hazael to inquire of the LORD through Elisha, the prophet from Israel: "Will I recover from this illness?" (2 Kings 8:8). When you're sick, friends, that's the only question in your head. Everything else can wait in line.

The answer is "You will surely recover." Those are the words Elisha, the LORD's prophet in Israel, gives Hazael to carry back: "Go and tell him, 'You will surely recover.'…" (2 Kings 8:10). Hazael, the king's man, hears that and probably thinks the news is good. But hold on, bakers, because Elisha isn't done. Keep reading the very next line.

The answer is die. Elisha tells Hazael to say the king will recover, "But the LORD has shown me that in fact he will die." (2 Kings 8:10). Two messages in one breath, friends. I think that's a lot for Hazael to carry back down the road.

The answer is weep. The man of God begins to weep (2 Kings 8:11). That's after Elisha fixes his gaze steadily on Hazael, the king's man, until Hazael becomes uncomfortable. A prophet staring is one thing, but a prophet staring and then crying is a whole different level. I'd have a lot of questions too.

The answer is that Elisha knows the evil Hazael will do to Israel. Hazael asks, "Why is my lord weeping?" and Elisha, the LORD's prophet in Israel, answers, "Because I know the evil you will do to the Israelites…" (2 Kings 8:12). The tears are for what's coming to Israel's people, and I think we can sit quietly with that for a moment, friends.

The answer is True. Hazael, the king's man, hears all of it and asks, "But how could your servant, a mere dog, do such a monstrous thing?" (2 Kings 8:13). He calls himself a mere dog, and he calls the deed monstrous. It's a heavy moment in the passage, friends. Elisha, the LORD's prophet in Israel, answers with something else the LORD has shown him.

The answer is that Hazael will be king over Aram. Elisha, the LORD's prophet in Israel, answers, "The LORD has shown me that you will be king over Aram." (2 Kings 8:13). Hazael, the king's man, asked how he could ever do such a thing, and the answer is this news about a crown. A servant carrying camel loads just got told he's going to wear the crown.

The answer is False. Ben-hadad, king of Aram, asks Hazael what Elisha said, and Hazael answers, "He told me that you would surely recover." (2 Kings 8:14). Elisha had also said the LORD showed him the king would die (2 Kings 8:10), but that part isn't in Hazael's answer. The very next day, friends, things move fast.
